title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Operating margins can be flattered by a single quarter's mix, but six years of balance-sheet deleveraging and free-cash-flow conversion never lie.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Vertiv's multi-year record from its 2020 SPAC listing through 9M 2026 shows two distinct regimes [4, 5, 6]. From 2020 to 2022, Vertiv operated as a leveraged, margin-compressed industrial [4, 5, 6]. From 2023 to 2026, it became a high-ROIC cash-compounding business [4, 5, 6]. Across 2020–2025, net sales more than doubled from $4,371 million to $10,229.9 million (18.5% 5-year CAGR), while GAAP operating profit rose over eightfold from $213.5 million to $1,829.7 million [1, 5].

web_blocks.caption: Vertiv Multi-Year Income & Cash Flow Forensics (FY2020–FY2025 Audited + 9M 2026 YTD)
web_blocks.takeaway: From FY2022 to FY2025, Vertiv expanded gross margin by 790 bps and lifted GAAP operating margin by 1,400 bps. Momentum continued in 9M 2026 with $3,878.0M gross profit (37.9%), $1,652.4M GAAP net income, and $2,230.3M adjusted FCF despite capex rising to $430.3M (4.2% of sales).

web_blocks.html: Vertiv overhauled its debt stack and reached a net cash position before closing UIG [41, 42]. On March 3, 2026, Vertiv issued $2,100.0 million of Senior Unsecured Notes due 2036 to 2066 at fixed coupons of 4.850% to 5.950% [41]. Proceeds plus cash repaid the $2,076.1 million floating-rate Term Loan due 2032 and settled $1.0 billion of SOFR swaps [41]. Vertiv also signed a $2,500.0 million Senior Unsecured Revolving Credit Facility due 2031 [41]. At September 30, 2026, cash and short-term investments totaled $3,711.7 million ($3,512.9 million cash plus $198.8 million ST investments) [41]. Against $2,928.5 million in carrying debt, Vertiv held $783.2 million in net cash prior to October's $1.45 billion UIG outlay [41, 43].

web_blocks.caption: Balance Sheet, Capital Efficiency & Working Capital Forensics (FY2020–Q3 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: By Q3 2026, Vertiv held $3,711.7M in cash and short-term investments against $2,928.5M carrying debt ($783.2M net cash) prior to paying $1.45B cash for UIG in October 2026, while inventories surged 125.8% YTD to $3,288.4M.

web_blocks.html: Four footnote items warrant close monitoring after the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q and October 2026 8-Ks [41, 43]. First, Level 3 earnout liabilities surged. PurgeRite's accrued earnout rose to $239.6 million at September 30, 2026, forcing $95.5 million in 9M operating expense remeasurement ($96.1 million across deals) [41]. Three 9M bolt-ons added $29.1 million in long-term earnouts, and UIG adds up to $1.15 billion in 12- and 24-month EBITDA earnouts [41, 43]. Second, goodwill ($2,279.6 million) and net intangibles ($1,736.1 million) reached $4,015.7 million—73.0% of $5,502.0 million equity—before UIG [41]. Item 4 also excludes PurgeRite, BMarko, Strategic Thermal Labs, and ThermoKey from 2026 ICFR testing [41]. Third, bank guarantees totaled $415.2 million, operating lease liabilities grew 36.0% YTD to $428.4 million, and warranty reserves rose 32.4% YTD to $57.2 million [41]. Fourth, Q3 diluted shares reached 392.7 million (385.03 million basic shares at quarter-end; 385.06 million at October 26) as 9M SBC climbed 30.5% to $50.5 million [41].

web_blocks.company: Corning Inc. (Optical Fiber & Photonics Buildout Cycle)
web_blocks.region_era: United States, 1999–2003 Telecom Infrastructure Capex Boom & Bust
web_blocks.mechanism: Mission-critical physical layer suppliers to a generational compute/network buildout expand factory capacity and backlog rapidly on multi-year customer forecasts, only to suffer severe utilization collapse and inventory write-downs when end-customers pause capex abruptly.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Corning's revenue fell from $7.1B (2000) to $3.1B (2003) as telecom carriers halted fiber deployment, swinging operating income to multi-billion-dollar losses and forcing plant closures before eventual multi-year recovery.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even indispensable physical-layer monopolies suffer sharp earnings air pockets if hyperscale AI capex pauses; investors must watch customer capex budgets, deferred revenue unwind, and fixed-cost absorption.

web_blocks.html: Working capital discipline remains a primary balance-sheet watch item [41]. At September 30, 2026, accounts receivable stood at $4,379.7 million net of $28.0 million credit allowances, and inventories hit $3,288.4 million [41]. Those balances were offset by $3,244.7 million in accounts payable and $4,120.5 million in current deferred revenue [41]. Customer deposits keep cash conversion strong, yet triple-digit inventory growth raises absorption risk if hyperscale shipments pause [41].

book_paragraphs: Numbers on a single-year income statement can flatter a cyclical business. That is why you and I always lay out at least six years of audited history side by side and inspect the balance sheet alongside the cash flow statement. When you do that for Vertiv from 2020 through 2025, you see two completely different companies.

From 2020 through 2022, Vertiv looked like a classic leveraged industrial struggling with inflation. Sales grew from 4.37 billion dollars to 5.69 billion dollars, yet gross margins fell every year—from 33.7 percent down to 28.4 percent. Free cash flow collapsed to negative 263.8 million dollars in 2022, and net debt reached 5.8 times EBITDA. Then came the reset. Between 2022 and 2025, Vertiv added 4.54 billion dollars of annual revenue, expanded gross margin by nearly 800 basis points to 36.3 percent, and multiplied GAAP operating profit more than eightfold from 223.4 million dollars to 1.83 billion dollars.

A closer look at the Q3 2026 footnotes reveals two offsetting forces. On the positive side, Vertiv replaced its floating-rate term loan in March 2026 with 2.10 billion dollars of fixed-rate investment-grade notes due 2036 through 2066. It also built 3.71 billion dollars in cash and short-term investments, creating a 783 million dollar net cash buffer before the UIG closing. On the risk side, contingent earnout liabilities now reach up to 1.4 billion dollars across PurgeRite, UIG, and recent deals. Goodwill and intangibles already equal 73 percent of equity before UIG, and inventories doubled to 3.29 billion dollars. Four newly acquired businesses also sit outside 2026 internal-control testing.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Repair and the Base-Rate Warning From History
paragraphs: Even more impressive than the income statement is what happened on the balance sheet. Vertiv held total debt roughly flat near 3.2 billion dollars while piling up 1.73 billion dollars in cash by year-end 2025. As EBITDA surged, Net Debt to EBITDA fell from 5.80 times in 2022 to just 0.62 times in 2025. Return on invested capital climbed from 3.6 percent to 22.3 percent—and nearly 24 percent on a trailing twelve-month basis. That financial cushion allowed Vertiv to pay roughly one billion dollars in cash for PurgeRite in late 2025 without jeopardizing its liquidity.

Still, history offers a sobering base rate whenever physical-infrastructure suppliers boom alongside a generational tech buildout. Think back to Corning during the 1999–2002 fiber-optic boom. Corning sold indispensable physical-layer hardware, expanded capacity on carrier forecasts, and then watched revenue drop from 7.1 billion dollars in 2000 to 3.1 billion dollars in 2003 when telecom capex froze. Vertiv is far healthier than 2000-era telecom suppliers, yet the lesson holds: keep one eye on hyperscaler capex budgets and receivables (111 days at year-end 2025) so an air pocket never catches you off guard.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: On pure operating fundamentals—22%+ ROIC, 140%+ FCF conversion, 0.62x net debt-to-EBITDA, and co-design incumbency in liquid cooling—Vertiv passes every quality gate as a structural compounder, tempered only by the cyclicality of hyperscale capital expenditure.

book_subsections.title: Separating Real Cash Compounding from Working-Capital Optics
paragraphs: Profit on an income statement is an accounting opinion; cash in the bank is a fact. Across FY2025, Vertiv turned $1,332.8 million of GAAP net income into $2,113.8 million of operating cash flow and $1,887.4 million of free cash flow—a 141.6 percent cash conversion ratio. Capital expenditures consumed just 2.2 percent of sales ($226.4 million), allowing Vertiv to de-lever from 5.80 times net debt-to-EBITDA in 2022 down to a conservative 0.62 times while still funding strategic acquisitions like PurgeRite.

Why, then, did we flag a watch item on working capital? Look at year-end FY2025 accounts receivable: $3,109.0 million, or 110.9 days sales outstanding. Part of that reflects heavy fourth-quarter shipment timing and large milestone billings with hyperscalers, cushioned by $3.63 billion in deferred revenue. Still, 111 days is a long collection cycle. Whenever a fast-growing equipment supplier carries triple-digit DSO, you and I must audit cash conversion every single quarter to make sure revenue growth is not being financed by looser customer credit.

book_subsections.title: De-Leveraging Without Diluting Shareholders
paragraphs: Vertiv repaired its balance sheet without dilutive stock offerings and then locked in long-term funding. Free cash flow reached 1,887.4 million dollars in 2025 and 2,230.3 million dollars on an adjusted basis in 9M 2026. In March 2026, management issued 2.10 billion dollars of fixed-rate senior unsecured notes due 2036 through 2066 at 4.85 to 5.95 percent. Those proceeds retired the 2.08 billion dollar floating-rate term loan, while a new 2.50 billion dollar revolving facility added liquidity.

By September 30, 2026, cash and short-term investments stood at 3,711.7 million dollars against 2,928.5 million dollars of carrying debt. That left a 783.2 million dollar net cash position ahead of the 1.45 billion dollar UIG closing. Diluted shares averaged 392.7 million in Q3 2026 (385.03 million basic at quarter-end; 385.06 million on October 26). Annual dilution remained modest even as nine-month stock-based compensation rose 30.5 percent to 50.5 million dollars.

book_subsections.title: Capex Lightness and the ROIC Advantage
paragraphs: Vertiv's historical 2.2 percent capex-to-sales ratio stepped up in 2026 as factory expansion accelerated. Nine-month 2026 capital spending including software totaled 430.3 million dollars, or 4.2 percent of sales. Full-year spending is guided near 4.0 percent.

Even at 4 percent capex intensity, Vertiv remains far lighter on fixed assets than foundries or utilities, sustaining trailing ROIC near 23.9 percent. Still, balance-sheet tracking now requires watching 4.02 billion dollars in goodwill and intangibles before UIG. Investors must also monitor 415.2 million dollars in performance bonds, 428.4 million dollars in lease liabilities, and up to 1.4 billion dollars in cash earnouts.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Our price-blind audit is now complete. Before ever looking at a single valuation multiple, you know what Vertiv builds, how it turns 100 dollars of sales into 18 dollars and 45 cents of free cash flow, and where its structural risks sit.
